Many users who recently came from Reddit seemed to think that voat would not be subject to the same kinds of pressures that have led that site to heavily censor its users. I believe that recent events, in particular the recent bans of subs on the basis of content and questionable legal threats, are quite telling. I don't mean this as doom and gloom, but as an observation of fact:

Voat cannot realistically provide a radical free-speech environment.

Such a platform can only be provided by a service whose operators are able to routinely violate the law without suffering ill consequences.

As far as I know, there is only one way for a popular service to accomplish this: by offering itself as a location-hidden service.

Some of you may wonder if this post is appropriate to /v/ideasforvoat , as voat is obviously not going to operate as a location-hidden service. I'm interested in discussing to what extent voat can offer a free-speech oriented platform and remain a viable, legal service - this is clearly relevant to the sub. But I'm also interested in discussing alternate services that could operate in the Tor network, to serve those who came here for a radical free-speech platform, and now must revise their expectations of voat.

What do you think? Is this just a temporary setback, and am I wrong about the impossiblity of an open and legal radical free-speech service? Is this the beginning of a more mature voat, which strikes a reasonable balance between free speech and self-preservatory content-based censorship? Or are you more cynical, and see this as the beginning of a slippery-slope towards becoming a lousy, advert filled, censored Reddit clone?
It was naive to think that voat could provide a robust, censorship-resistant platform. Only a hidden service could do that, today.

I don't see the Silk Road example as a problem for offering hidden services with questionable legal status. Tor is slow. But the network is actually remarkably stable these days. It is too slow for rapid Reddit-style browsing, though. But I think it is fast enough for a discussion site.
